TLCConcept.showAs: The Coroners and Justice Act 2009 (Commencement No. 21) Order 2023

formula.name: enactingText
formula.p:
The Secretary of State makes this in exercise of the power conferred by section 182(5) of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009
2009 c. 25; there are amendments to section 182 which are not relevant to this Order. .

content.p: This Order may be cited as the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 (Commencement No. 21) Order 2023.
This Order extends to England and Wales.

article.heading: Commencement of provisions of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009

intro.p: The following provisions of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 come into force on 1st October 2023—

content.p:
section 19 (medical examiners: supplementary)
Section 19 was amended by section 54(1) and (2) of the Health and Social Care Act 2012 (c. 7) (“the 2012 Act”), and by section 169(2) of the Health and Care Act 2022 (c. 31) (“the 2022 Act”). Section 54 of the 2012 Act was repealed by section 169(6) of the 2022 Act. , and

section 20 (medical certificate of cause of death)
Section 20 was amended by section 54(1) and (3) of the 2012 Act, by section 169(3) of the 2022 Act, and by S.I. 2018/378. .

content.block: Department of Health and Social Care

blockContainer.heading: Explanatory Note
blockContainer.subheading: (This note is not part of the )
blockContainer.p: This Order commences sections 19 and 20 of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 (c. 25) on 1st October 2023.
Section 19 makes provision in relation to the appointment of medical examiners and confers powers on appropriate Ministers to make regulations in relation to medical examiners.
Section 20 confers a power on the Secretary of State to make regulations in relation to the preparation of medical certificates of cause of death.
